title: Autoscaler oscillation playbook — scratch
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Noted recurring "ping-pong" in Dedicated GPU pool A (us-west-2) for customer cluster: repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down within 30–90s window. Looks like scaler is overreacting to transient bursts, warmup penalty makes the downscale harmful (cold GPUs + model load).
- Symptoms: throughput drops -> attach new node -> new node reported healthy but slow for first 90s (model cold init) -> CPU/memory spikes on orchestrator -> autoscaler sees reduced per-node utilization -> triggers scale-down -> evict -> latency spike and repeat.
- Impact: customer-facing tail latency 95/99 up to 3–5x; cost wasted on sub-1min GPU churn.

Raw observations / timeline snippets:
- 2026-02-18T03:12:07Z autoscaler: Received metric event: route=chat-model-7, rps=120, last_10s_qps=95
- 2026-02-18T03:12:15Z scale-manager: scale-up request -> poolA +1 (type p4d)
- 2026-02-18T03:13:40Z node-init: model-fetch complete, kv-cache empty, baseline latency=350ms
- 2026-02-18T03:14:20Z autoscaler: observed node_util=14% (aggregate), decision=scale-down poolA -1
- 2026-02-18T03:14:31Z eviction: draining pod chat-model-7-5 -> rescheduled onto remaining nodes -> 99th latency spike seen at 03:14:45

Commands I ran while investigating:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=poolA --context=redwood-prod
- kubectl describe hpa chat-model-7 -n inference (our internal shim exposes HPA-like metrics)
- curl -sS http://metrics.internal/poolA/recent | jq '.autoscaler_events | last(20)'
- ssh to node (i-0abcde) and check systemd logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-inference-agent -n 200
- docker logs for model container: docker logs --tail 200 rinf-chatv7

Commands / snippets that helped reproduce locally (dev stack):
- stress load generator (rlimit): ./tools/load-gen --qps 120 --burst 30 --duration 6m --route chat-model-7
- local autoscaler sim: python infra/tools/autoscaler_sim.py --policy aggressive --metrics-file ./samples/short_burst.json

Error / log excerpts (copy-paste):
- [autoscaler] 2026-02-18T03:14:20Z decision: scale_down poolA reasons=[low_node_util:14%, short_term_drop:true]
- [node-agent] 2026-02-18T03:13:06Z model-loader WARN model-fetch retry #3 (timeout 8s)
- [serving-runtime] 2026-02-18T03:13:48Z kv-cache: miss_count=1 priming_started=true

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Aggressive reactive policy: the autoscaler uses a short smoothing window (30s) so it treats the post-burst cool-down as sustained low demand. With warmup latency, scale-down is premature.
2) New node readiness metric is optimistic: node marked Ready after container is running but before model weights/KV cache primed. We treat "nodeReady" as sufficient for serving.
3) Placement packing + pod eviction threshold: eviction prefers consolidating small loads which amplifies utilization variance causing cascade.
4) Metric noise / sampling lag between metrics pipeline and decision loop results in oscillation when bursts are frequent.

Immediate mitigations tried (notes):
- Increased minPoolSize for poolA from 2 -> 3 for 24h (manual override). Observed reduced churn but higher baseline cost.
- Bumped cooldown window to 180s in the experimental policy branch (--cooldown-secs=180). This reduced oscillation in sim runs.
- Implemented temporary server-side gate: do not scale down nodes that are < 5m old AND have had a model-load event in last 2m. (This is a hack; risky long-term.)
- Prewarm suggestion: attempted to mark new nodes "serving=false" until model priming hook completes (model-loader emits primed=true). Integration took 30m to implement in dev and looks promising.

Things to test / experiments to run (next):
- Canary the model-primed readiness: add an additional readiness probe that only flips when model KV cache > X entries OR model health endpoint /primed==true. Measure time-to-primed across GPUs (p4d vs a100).
- Run long-run sim with real burst traces (from metrics archive): ./infra/tools/autoscaler_sim.py --trace traces/2026-02-poolA.json --policy conservative --grace=240
- Try hysteresis vs smoothing comparison: smoothing(window=120s) vs cooldown(grace=240s) to see which reduces tail latency with minimal cost increase.
- Evaluate packing policy: change bin-packing threshold to 0.7 and observe if utilization variance reduces.

Longer-term ideas / proposals:
- Introduce "primed readiness" at platform level. Autoscaler should consider primed state before counting node as fully available for downscale computations.
- Add a cost-per-eviction metric to optimizer. If evicting a node causes a tail-latency penalty > X for > Y minutes, treat as a failed scale-down.
- Predictive ramping: short-term forecast (30–120s) using the route's recent burstiness score; if forecast indicates more bursts treat scale decisions conservatively.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Does Dedicated scheduler surface model-load progress? Currently model-loader logs, but no structured metric. TODO: add /metrics model_loader_load_seconds and primed_gauge. (Owner: Samantha)
- Q: What is the minimal cooldown that stops the oscillation without doubling cost? Run binary search on cooldown window in sim. (Owner: Marcus)
- TODO: Attach the 02-18 trace to INC-2026-87 (I think Linear ticket already has partial logs).
- TODO: Create small perf test comparing A100 vs P4d cold-start times using exact model version v7-2026-01. (Owner: Rajiv)

Notes to self / rough timeline for rollout:
- Week 1: instrument model-loader -> metrics (prometheus) + add primed readiness probe (dev only).
- Week 2: run sims with historical traces and tune cooldown/hysteresis.
- Week 3: Canary primed-readiness + conservative policy in us-west-2 poolA (2 small customers) -> monitor 99th latency and cost.
- Week 4+: If stable, roll to other pools and bake into scheduler config.

Random scratch ideas (low friction):
- Use lightweight model warmers that run small synthetic prompts on new nodes as part of post-deploy hook (cost small vs full model load).
- Heuristic: prefer scale-down candidates that have had "no model loads in last 15m" to avoid evicting nodes that were recently primed.

References / links I keep hitting:
- INC-2026-87 (ticket) - customer report + initial logs
- GH-PR-4821 - autoscaler cooldown experiment branch
- CONFLUENCE-POOL-AUTOSCALER-RUNBOOK - current runbook (does not mention primed readiness)

If I forget: step 0 = add primed metric. step 1 = cooldown tuning. step 2 = primed-readiness canary.

End of scratch notes.

(If reading later: this is intentionally messy. Many TODOs are half-formed — prioritize instrumentation first.)
